title: Egg sandwich on white bread, with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: An egg sandwich on white bread with cheese is a simple dish made of a boiled or fried egg, melted or sliced cheese, and two slices of white bread. It is often served hot, with the cheese slightly melted and the bread toasted to a golden crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich originated in the United States in the early 1920s as a quick breakfast for workers.
White bread provides a fast source of carbohydrates, while the egg supplies a complete protein with essential amino acids.
Cheese used is often cheddar or gouda, which melt well and give the sandwich a distinctive flavor.
Variations may include added vegetables (tomato, lettuce) or sauces (mayonnaise, mustard).
Egg sandwiches are a staple in school cafeterias and fast‑food menus.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: One egg provides about 6 g of high‑quality protein, important for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Egg yolk is one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium, essential for strong teeth and bones.

items.title: Energy‑dense
items.content: The combination of carbs from bread and fats from cheese offers quick and sustained energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B2, B6, and B12 vitamins, which aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs or cheese.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: High glycemic index of white bread
items.content: White bread can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Trans fats in processed cheese
items.content: Certain processed cheeses may contain trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is usually served hot: toast the bread lightly, cook the egg to your liking (hard‑boiled, soft‑boiled, fried), place the cheese on top to melt, then assemble. Optional additions include lettuce, tomato, or your favorite sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in plastic film. Keep bread and cheese separate in airtight containers.
